To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) attitudes to science are a complex construct and are difficult to measure; 2) there are a range of factors which affect attitudes to science, but the two most significant are gender and the quality and type of teaching; 3) there is a need for research to explore the nature of teaching that engages pupils and motivates them to study science.
the attitudes of pupils towards science are influenced by many factors, including gender, teachers, the curriculum, cultural factors and other variables.
the literature suggests that attitudes to science are a complex construct that are influenced by a number of factors, including gender and the quality and nature of science teaching.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of a programme designed to improve pupils’ attitudes to science.
how pupils’ attitudes to science are formed, and how these attitudes are related to the quality of teaching and to the nature of school science itself.
how to raise students’ interest in school science, and the implications of our findings for the teaching and learning of science.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there is a need to understand the nature of students’ attitudes towards studying science, to identify the key factors that influence them and to develop appropriate teaching strategies to enhance them.
there are a range of factors that influence attitudes to science and that the most important of those factors are gender and quality of teaching.
there are many influences on attitudes to science, and that these are complex and interrelated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is no single factor that can explain why students choose or not to study science at GCSE.
attitudes are a complex construct that are influenced by many factors and which in turn influence the way in which students engage with science.

there is an urgent need to develop a better understanding of students’ attitudes to school science and their implications if we are to understand and remedy the decline in the numbers choosing to study it.
The main takeaway from our work is that
attitudes to science are important and that there is a need for further research to better understand their nature and the factors that influence them.

the literature points to the need for a more nuanced approach to the study of students’ attitudes to school science, one which takes account of the complex interplay of factors that affect their attitudes.
attitudes to science are a complex and multidimensional construct and that the measurement of them is not without its own challenges.
